alt: Clients connect to two leaf switches, leaf A and leaf B, joined by a 2×100G ISL. One vyrn-seq box hangs off both: NIC0, NIC1 and NIC4 on leaf A, NIC2, NIC3 and NIC5 on leaf B, with data nodes, the observer and one grandmaster (GM-1 primary, GM-2 backup) on each side. Metro path A leaves from NIC4 and metro path B from NIC5 toward facilities F2…Fn, so each order-stream path rides its own switch.

The cgroup v2 tree under -.slice: init.scope, system.slice (sshd, journald, ptp4l, phc2sys, vyrn-timemon, vyrn-admin) and user.slice all have AllowedCPUs=HK and converge on core 51, the housekeeping core of a REF box. vyrn.slice alone has AllowedCPUs=0-63 and spans the whole 64-core strip; each of its threads then pins itself to one core from its core map.

A timeline of vyrn-seq start-up on HK: parse config and topology, mlockall and prctl, then spawn one pinned thread per core-map entry. A stack of per-core cards shows steps a to f running in parallel on every core, including touching every 4 KiB of every region so all first-touch faults happen now. After READY, the control core verifies the baselines, each core calls seal(), sd_notify fires, and in steady state minflt and majflt must not change.

Four builds converge on one link: the C shim and vendored libciul compile with clang -flto=thin to bitcode, vendored DPDK with its mlx5/ena PMDs builds with meson and b_lto, and rustc emits an .rlib with linker-plugin-lto. All of them feed lld with LLVM LTO, which emits the single vyrn-seq binary. Notes record that PMDs link --whole-archive and that rdma-core is not linked.

Inside the facility, GNSS feeds GM-1 and GM-2, which feed leaf A and leaf B (PTP boundary clocks), and leaf A feeds NIC0's PHC, which ptp4l disciplines with hardware stamps. From NIC0, phc2sys fans out to NIC1–NIC3 PHCs, to NIC4 and NIC5 (replication, rx_ts unused) and to CLOCK_REALTIME / CLOCK_TAI, which drives the TAI map. vyrn-timemon measures cross-NIC skew with two-way probes and builds TSC↔PHC lines with PTM at 100 Hz, because skew between one box's PHCs is a fairness error.

The time-state machine: UNSYNC goes to LOCKED once ptp4l is s2 and the GM offset and skew stay within bounds for 60 s, LOCKED and HOLDOVER move between each other on GM loss and return, and HOLDOVER falls back to UNSYNC after PLT_HOLDOVER_MAX_S (300 s). SKEWED and MAPERR can be entered from any state and return to UNSYNC once their thresholds hold for 60 s. Canary marks the two states that may sequence, LOCKED and HOLDOVER; FREERUN stands apart, lab and standalone CONSUMER only.

A client sends every packet twice: copy 1 to vyrn-seq, which emits the order stream (ORDER, HASH and HEADER frames) on two paths at 3.3 GB/s per path, and copy 2 to the session's data home, vyrn-data, which sends data frames at 19.2 GB/s to each replica. vyrn-replica joins the two by (session, pkt_seq) and checks pkt_hash and data_root; joined, they make block h.

Lane l pushes R_pkt and R_hash8 records to stream-A (core 4) or stream-B (core 7) in CCD 0, and R_hash32 to the order hasher on core 50, which also reads the frame rings. The BBO core 2 writes R_step once and three cursors read it (core 50, core 7, core 4), and it hands fills over R_fill_X to the TX cores 3, 5 and 0. The stream cores publish released[A], released[B] and LaneCut back to the lanes, and a fill goes out only when released[A] ≥ need_A(s) and released[B] ≥ need_B(s).

The data box's ingest pipeline as a two-row assembly line: RX queue (RSS by session, ~12 cores at peak), parse header (16 B), MAC check (K_seq in BASE, K_com in CHAIN), dedupe by (session, pkt_seq), full BLAKE3 (32 B kept, pkt_hash 8 B), store into a RAM ring with an index, and fan-out of data frames to every voter and the warm standby. Reject chutes show what each check drops: invalid packets, failed MACs reported as DataBadMac, repeats with the same hash, and CopyConflict when a repeat carries a new hash.

Catch-up after a restart: from t0 the replica subscribes to live frames and data and votes at once, shown as a violet votes track that runs the whole time. In parallel it fetches the newest snapshot at or before the newest RootCert (local NVMe, else peers via REPAIR, else archive), verifies it, fetches and verifies finalized blocks striped across peers, and replays at full speed. Once replay lag is at most REP_LIVE_LAG_MS (10 ms) it is caught up and a second track, root votes, begins.

The byte layout of REP_BlockRecord, a 4 KiB-aligned record written to drive h mod 12. Bytes 0–24 are drawn to scale (magic "PBBLK001", height, epoch, tenure, kind, reserved); bytes 24–256 hold the 190-byte BlockHeader, four 4-byte length fields and 26 reserved bytes. From byte 256 come the order bytes, the pkt_hash list, the data bytes, the unavailable (session, pkt_seq) list and padding to 4 KiB, and dashed links tie each length field to the part it sizes.
